morgan: Quick Q — working on the acme corp private deployment observability. Where are we surface-ing the customer's Prometheus/Grafana endpoints for SRE/CS to poke? Need to share with their infra team.

ravi: For that deployment we expose read-only Grafana links via the customer portal (AuthN via SSO token). There's also a private Prometheus `remote_read`/`remote_write` endpoint we forward to our central long-term store.

morgan: Got it — can you paste the portal link + the firewall requirements? Customer asked what IPs/ports to open.

ravi: Portal: https://portal.redwood.internal/customers/acme/grafana (internal)
Firewall: outbound TCP 443 to `proxy.redwood-internal:443` for Grafana embed; for Prometheus remote_write we accept connections from the customer's scrape targets on TCP 9091 (proxy) — they should allow our egress to `10.10.20.0/24` (private peering) or the NAT IP if they use internet egress. I'll add details in the infra doc.

elsa: Also FYI — if the customer wants direct access to their own Grafana instance inside the VPC (not the portal embed) we can create a bastion jump with ephemeral certs. That's a manual support flow (CS ticket).

kevin: Customer asked about pushing OTLP traces/logs to Redwood instead of scraping Prom. Is there a recommended collector config we give them?

ravi: Yes — we recommend using the OpenTelemetry Collector. Minimal sample for OTLP over HTTP to our collector:
```yaml
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
      http:
exporters:
  otlphttp:
    endpoint: "https://collector.redwood.internal/v1/otel"
    headers:
      x-api-key: "<CUSTOMER_API_KEY>"
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      exporters: [otlphttp]
    logs:
      receivers: [otlp]
      exporters: [otlphttp]
```
Tell them to swap in the API key from the portal (Settings -> API keys).

morgan: Nice. Anything special for Prometheus -> remote_write relabeling so metrics don't collide across tenants?

ravi: Yes — we require a tenant label. Example `relabel_configs` snippet for Prometheus `remote_write`:
```
relabel_configs:
  - source_labels: [__address__]
    target_label: instance
  - replacement: "acme-corp"
    target_label: tenant_id
```
We also run a quota+ingress filter so mismatched `tenant_id` values get rejected — double-check their scrape configs.

kevin: If they want logs forwarded via OTLP -> do we support logfile tailing (fluentbit) to OTLP?

ravi: Yup. Recommend Fluent Bit with the `stdout`->OTLP plugin (or use the Fluent Forwarder to our collector). We have a reference fluent-bit config in the docs: https://redwood.internal/docs/private/otlp-fluentbit (internal).

morgan: Can someone confirm where the Grafana dashboard defs live (to share a permalink to the CPU/latency dashboards)? I need the dashboard UID.

ravi: Customer dashboards are created under the `acme-corp` org in Grafana. UID for the standard infra dashboard: `Zk7k1H9A`. Link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/Zk7k1H9A/acme-infra

elsa: I'll attach the onboarding checklist to the CS ticket: include keys they need (API key, grafana embed token), firewall table, and the relabel examples.

morgan: Thanks. Last ask — alert tuning: can we recommend a starting alertset? CPU > 85% for 5m, memory RSS > 75% with 10m window, scrape failures > 3 in 5m. Is that OK?

ravi: Those are fine as baseline. Add a `tenant_id` filter to the alert rules so they only fire for acme-corp metrics. We'll also push a canary alert rule in their Grafana org labeled `acme-defaults`.

oncall-bot: Note: there's a scheduled maintenance for `collector.redwood.internal` at 2026-02-12T03:00Z that may affect ingestion for ~15m. See: https://status.redwood.internal/incidents/collector-maint-20260212

morgan: Good catch — I'll flag that in the onboarding docs when I send instructions. Anything else?

kevin: Nope, I'll open the CS ticket and attach links + the OTLP snippet. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
